question.text: During the qualitative analysis of salt with cation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math>, addition of a reagent <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mfenced></math> to alkaline solution of the salt gives a bright red precipitate. The reagent <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mfenced></math> and the cation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mfenced></math> present respectively are :

solution.text:
During the qualitative analysis of salt with cation Ni2+, addition of a reagent Dimethylglyoxime to alkaline solution of the salt gives a bright red precipitate according to the following reaction. So, The reagent X and the cation y2+ respectively are Dimethylglyoxime and Ni2+
